# Question 1: Using the geom_tile() function, visualise the luminescence across the plate. Do there appear to be any spatial patterns in this data?

## Load packages

```{r}
# Load tidyverse and ggplot2
library(tidyverse)
library(ggplot2)

```

## Prepare plate1 dataset to use geom_tile()

plate1 contains luminescence (RLU) values, and will therefore be used to answer Q1

```{r}
# geom_tile requires plate1 to be in long format

plate1_long <- plate1 |> 
  pivot_longer(
    # collapse all columns into 1 column except plate_row 
    cols = -plate_row, 
    # all columns collapsed into 1 column named "plate_col"
    names_to = "plate_col", 
    # all RLU values in column named "luminescence"
    values_to = "luminescence"
  )

# Check that pivot_longer() worked 
View(plate1_long)

# Convert plate_row and plate_col values from character to numeric 
# using parse_number() for 'tidier' data

plate1_long <- plate1_long |> 
  mutate(
    # keep numbers after "row"
    plate_row = parse_number(plate_row),
    # keep numbers after "col"
    plate_col = parse_number(plate_col))

# Check rows and columns have numeric values 
View(plate1_long)
```

## Visualise luminescence as heatmap

Loading esquisse

```{r}
# Install and load esquisse

remotes::install_github("dreamRs/esquisse")

library(esquisse)

esquisse::esquisser(plate1_long)
```

Copy/paste code from esquisse below:

```{r}
ggplot(plate1_long) +
  
  aes(x = plate_col, y = plate_row, fill = luminescence) +
  geom_tile(
    colour = "grey50", 
    linewidth = 0.1
  ) +
  scale_fill_viridis_c(option = "viridis", direction = 1) +
  # label every 2nd column number at the top to avoid over-cluttering
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(1, 48, by = 2), expand = c(0, 0), position = "top") +
  # use scale_y_reverse() to get rows to start from 1 at the top like a plate
  scale_y_reverse(breaks = seq(1, 32, by = 2), expand = c(0, 0)) +
  coord_equal() +
  # add title, axes titles and legend
  labs(
    x = "Column",
    y = "Row",
    title = "Luminescence across 1536-well plate after 24h MPP treatment",
    fill = "Luminescence (RLU)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(size = 12L,
                              face = "bold",
                              hjust = 0.5),
    axis.title.y = element_text(size = 10L),
    axis.title.x = element_text(size = 10L)
  )
```

## Answer

There doesn't appear to be any spatial patterns in the data. Wells with higher RLU values seem to be randomly scattered throughout the 1536-well plate.

# Question 2: Which compounds are statistically significantly associated with increased neuronal viability after MPP exposure? Ensure that you check your assumptions.

## Incorporating plate_meta dataset

```{r}
library(dplyr)

# convert plate_meta into long format
cmpd_long <- plate_meta |> 
  pivot_longer(
    # collapse all columns into 1 column except plate_row 
    cols = -plate_row, 
    # all columns collapsed into 1 column named "plate_col"
    names_to = "plate_col", 
    # all RLU values in column named "luminescence"
    values_to = "cmpd"
  )

# Check that pivot_longer() worked
View(cmpd_long)

# Convert plate_row and plate_col values from character to numeric so that cmpd_long 
# can be joined to plate1_long
cmpd_long <- cmpd_long |> 
  mutate(
    # keep numbers after "row"
    plate_row = parse_number(plate_row),
    # keep numbers after "col"
    plate_col = parse_number(plate_col))

# Combine plate1_long and cmpd_long using left_join
combined_data <- plate1_long |> 
  left_join(cmpd_long, 
            by = c("plate_row", "plate_col"))

# Check that left_join() worked
View(cmpd_long)
```

## Tidying combined_data

```{r}
# Replace cmpd column with two new columns for the cmpd number and 
# condition (ctrl/test)
combined_data <- combined_data |> 
  separate(
    cmpd,
    into = c("prefix", "cmpd", "cond"),
    sep = "_"
  ) |> 
  # remove prefix
  select(-prefix)

# Check two new columns contain the cmpd number and the condition type
View(combined_data)

# Check that each compound (test/ctrl) has 4 replicates
combined_data  |> 
  count(cmpd, cond) |> 
  filter(n != 4)
```

## Analyse how average luminescence changes between conditions (test vs. ctrl) for each compound

```{r}
summary <- combined_data |> 
  group_by(cmpd, cond) |> 
  summarise(
    mean_lum = mean(luminescence),
    sd_lum = sd(luminescence),
    n = n(),
    .groups = "drop"
    )
# Check summary dataset created includes mean_lum and sd_lum columns
View(summary)

comparison_data <- summary |> 
  select(cmpd, cond, mean_lum) |> 
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = cond,
    values_from = mean_lum
  ) |> 
  mutate(
    difference = test - ctrl,
    percent_change = 100 * (test - ctrl) / ctrl
  )

View(comparison_data)
```

# Statistical analysis - normality

Install and load "rstatix" package

```{r}
install.packages("rstatix")
library(rstatix)
```

Generate Q-Q plots to accept/reject normality

```{r}
# Determine residuals for each compound and condition from the group's mean
residual_data <- combined_data |>
  group_by(cmpd, cond) |>
  mutate(
    residual = luminescence - mean(luminescence)
  ) |>
  ungroup()

# Check that residual column was added  
View(residual_data)

# Generate Q-Q plots for control compounds and test compounds 
ggplot(residual_data, aes(sample = residual)) +
  geom_qq() +
  geom_qq_line() +
  facet_wrap(~cond) +
  labs(
    title = "Q-Q plots of within-group residuals",
    x = "Theoretical quantiles",
    y = "Residual luminescence (RLU)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```

```{r}
# Confirm normality with Shapiro-Wilk test
shapiro_results <- combined_data |>
  group_by(cmpd, cond) |>
  summarise(
    shapiro_p = shapiro.test(luminescence)$p.value,
    .groups = "drop"
  )

shapiro_results |>
  summarise(
    total_tests = n(),
    p_below_05 = sum(shapiro_p < 0.05),
    percentage = mean(shapiro_p < 0.05) * 100
  )
```

Q-Q plots .

Analysis performing Shapiro-Wilk tests confirm that only 26 (6.7%) of the 192 control and test compounds

Data are normally distributed and we can conduct t-test.

```{r}
welch_results <- combined_data |>
  group_by(cmpd) |>
  t_test(
    luminescence ~ cond,
    var.equal = FALSE,
    alternative = "less",
    p.adjust.method = "none"
  )

welch_results <- welch_results |>
  ungroup() |>
  adjust_pvalue(method = "BH")
```

```{r}
significant_compounds <- welch_results |>
  filter(p.adj < 0.05) |>
  arrange(p.adj)
```
